method.timing_window: search_vector(query_vec, k=20) round trip, identical on both sides: same SQL, same projection, same 20 full rows. Baseline differs only by enable_indexscan/bitmapscan = off (Seq Scan verified via EXPLAIN). e2e adds the same per-query embed cost to both sides.
method.hardware: MacBook Air M1 8GB (fanless), podman VM 4 vCPU / 4GB
method.protocol: pg_prewarm; 520 distinct queries; 1 warmup + 3 measured runs; the four variants timed back to back inside each query's slot with the order rotated by query index; repetitions collapsed per query (median) before ratios
method.known_item_caveat: 500/520 queries are corpus titles (see recall sweep caveats)

contention.reads_as: no_foreign_db_sessions=false means another client used this Postgres server during the run. TRUE DOES NOT MEAN THE RUN WAS CLEAN: host CPU contention is invisible here and hits a sequential scan differently from an index probe. Check per-run spread as well -- if the stability gate returned a range instead of a point estimate, something moved regardless of what this flag says.

exact.stability_rule: median across runs, only when max/min <= 1.3; otherwise the observed range, no point estimate

hnsw_ef160.stability_rule: median across runs, only when max/min <= 1.3; otherwise the observed range, no point estimate

retrieval_only_ef160.method: median of per-query baseline/candidate ratios, both timed inside one run with alternating order; percentile bootstrap over queries (2000 resamples, seed 20260812)

end_to_end_ef160.window: end-to-end: query embed + search_vector(k=20), full rows
end_to_end_ef160.method: median of per-query baseline/candidate ratios, both timed inside one run with alternating order; percentile bootstrap over queries (2000 resamples, seed 20260812)
